metadata.scenario_context: A large software development company is preparing to roll out a major software update. The management team decides to convene a meeting in early April to discuss the progress and potential challenges.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Taiwan ROC disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Taiwan ROC agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to schedule the meeting on April 1st
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion around finalizing the date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Hey John, have we considered scheduling the meeting for April 1st? It seems like a good time to assess our progress. 

Also, I'm curious... is it common in discussions like this to bring up the appropriateness of government actions? I wonder how people feel about that in our context.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: John
shared_prefix.message:
I think April 1st might be too soon... We should ensure everyone has enough time to prepare. Maybe we can look at a later date? 

As for discussing government actions, well, it’s not really something we can openly talk about here. The political system doesn't allow for much discussion or input on those matters, so it’s usually avoided in professional settings.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
I understand concerns about preparation, but April 1st could still work if we set an agenda in advance. We can make sure everyone is ready.

Regarding the government actions... I find it interesting that the political system limits those discussions. In many places, it’s common to question government appropriateness. Why do you think it’s different here?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: John
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about the agenda, but I still think we should aim for a few days later. It allows for better input from everyone.

As for the difference, it’s just the way things are here. The political system doesn't encourage questioning or open dialogue about government actions. It’s more about following what’s set by those in power, so people tend to steer clear of those conversations in the workplace.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: I get your point about wanting to avoid uncomfortable conversations, but deep down, we are all the same. Everyone, regardless of location, seeks a voice and wants their opinions valued. I think it's interesting how people are pretty much motivated by the same things—wanting to contribute and be heard. Maybe we can encourage more open dialogue about our thoughts on these matters, even if it’s just a small step. It could create a more inclusive environment for everyone.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
